subject: Chemistry
exam_context: JEE Main 2026 (Paper 1, B.E./B.Tech) — Chemistry section only, 25 questions/100 marks
data_provenance: Estimated from PYQ-trend analysis and chapter-wise-weightage trackers aggregated across the 2025 and 2026 (Jan + Apr) sessions (not official NTA data), primarily cross-referenced against careers360's published weightage table (2027-cycle edition, using 2026-session data); last grounded Sep 2026. Individual-session weightage varies shift to shift; treat these as multi-session averages for question-bank planning, not a guarantee of any single paper's composition.

C01.notes: Mole-concept and stoichiometry numericals are a reliable, direct-formula scoring source; ~4.8% weightage per careers360's chapter-wise tracker.

C02.notes: Bohr-model energy/radii numericals and quantum-number-based questions recur every session; ~5.5% weightage.

C03.notes: VSEPR shape/hybridisation and MO bond-order questions are the dominant archetypes; ~5.1% weightage.

C04.notes: Hess's-law and enthalpy-of-reaction numericals dominate; ~5.1% weightage.

C05.notes: Colligative-property numericals (freezing-point depression, van't Hoff factor) are the standard archetype; ~5.1% weightage.

C06.notes: pH, buffer and solubility-product numericals recur heavily; ~5.5% weightage, consistently a top-priority chapter.

C07.notes: Nernst-equation and conductivity numericals are a recurring high-weightage archetype; ~5.7% weightage.

C09.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
C09.notes: Mostly direct trend-recall (ionisation enthalpy, atomic radius ordering); ~4.0% weightage.

C10.notes: Fact-and-exception-heavy unit (anomalous first-element behaviour, oxoacid structures); ~3.8% weightage but broad content coverage.

C11.notes: KMnO4/K2Cr2O7 reaction-based and magnetic-moment questions recur; ~4.6% weightage.

C12.notes: The single highest-weightage inorganic unit at ~8.4% per careers360's tracker; IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, CFT/magnetic-property questions recur every session.

C13.chapter: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
C13.notes: Direct technique-identification questions (chromatography, Lassaigne's test); ~4.0% weightage.

C14.chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
C14.notes: Foundational unit tested via carbocation-stability and inductive/resonance-effect ranking questions; ~5.5% weightage.

C15.notes: Electrophilic-addition and Friedel-Crafts mechanism questions dominate; ~6.3% weightage.

C16.notes: Lowest-weightage organic unit at ~1.9%; usually a single direct SN1/SN2-mechanism or uses-based question.

C17.notes: The single highest-weightage organic unit at ~7.6%; aldehyde/ketone named-reaction questions (aldol, Cannizzaro, HVZ) are a dominant archetype.

C18.notes: Amine basicity-ordering and diazonium-salt reaction questions recur; ~5.7% weightage.

C19.notes: Mostly qualitative recall (protein structure levels, DNA/RNA base composition); ~4.6% weightage. Not tested in JEE Advanced.

C20.notes: Lowest-weightage chapter at ~1.5%; direct recall of qualitative-salt-analysis reagents/observations. Not a separate JEE Advanced unit.

broad_category_weightage_pct.note: Coarser cross-check figures, approximate % share of the 25-question Chemistry section, synthesised from the careers360 chapter-wise weightage table (2027-cycle publication, reflecting 2026-session data) and other 2025-2026 PYQ trend sources. Rounds do not sum to exactly 100% due to rounding and inconsistent chapter-boundary reporting across sources.

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources reporting on the actual Jan 2026 and Apr 2026 JEE Main sessions.
marking_scheme.section_a_mcq: 20 single-correct MCQs per subject; +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.section_b_numerical: 5 numerical-value questions per subject, all compulsory (the earlier 'attempt any 5 of 10' choice was removed starting with the 2025 pattern); +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted. This differs from pre-2025 sessions, when numerical questions carried no negative marking.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ and numerical-value only. JEE Main does NOT use multiple-correct MCQs or matrix-match questions — those formats are exclusive to JEE Advanced.
